 Advertisement Massachusetts 2026 midterm election guide: Races, ballot questions and voting info
 Advertisement Updated: 6:24 PM EDT Oct 30, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Phil Tenser Digital Media Manager Sharman Sacchetti Political Reporter and Co-Host of WCVB’s “On The Record” Ed Harding Anchor Massachusetts 2026 midterm election guide: Races, ballot questions and voting info
 Updated: 6:24 PM EDT Oct 30, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Phil Tenser Digital Media Manager Sharman Sacchetti Political Reporter and Co-Host of WCVB’s “On The Record” Ed Harding Anchor NEEDHAM, Mass. — Massachusetts voters face a packed ballot Tuesday, with nine statewide questions—the most to appear on a Bay State ballot since 1918—alongside high-profile races for governor, U.S. Senate and all nine seats in the U.S. House. Here’s what to know before you vote. 
 U.S. Senate race
 After a bruising primary, Sen. Ed Markey is seeking a third term in Tuesday's general election against Republican attorney John Deaton and two other challengers.
 Advertisement Deaton, who fell short in his challenge against Sen. Elizabeth Warren two years ago, said he believed that the experience from his previous campaign improved his chances this time around.
 Markey survived contested party primaries in 2020 and again this year. This time, the 80-year-old incumbent promised that, if he wins in November, the next term would be his last.
 "This is going to be my last term," Markey said. "And I'm going to make it count."
 "I'm not running because Ed's too old and he's been there too long," Deaton said. "But my ideas on solving problems are just better than his."
 Gubernatorial race
 Gov. Maura Healey, a Democrat, is running for a second term. She's being challenged by Mike Minogue, a Republican former biotech executive, and an independent candidate.
 During their final debate , hosted by WCVB and a consortium of partners, the topic of conversation repeatedly turned to affordability.
 Healey argued that high prices are a direct result of the war with Iran and tried to link Minogue to President Donald Trump's policies.
 Minogue blamed high energy costs on Healey, arguing that she stopped a natural gas pipeline project while she was attorney general. He said that he would incorporate natural gas and nuclear energy into his energy strategy and argued that wind energy is too expensive to deserve a state investment.
 Massachusetts Governor's race heats up in final days before election Ballot questions
 The nine questions tie the record for the most ever to appear on Bay State ballots since the 1918 amendment to the state constitution that created the procedure.
 Topics for the ballot questions this year range from the workings of government and elections to whether state laws about firearms and marijuana should be repealed.
 Massachusetts Question 1: 2026 ballot question asks voters about expanding public records law Massachusetts Question 2: Collective bargaining for CPCS employees on the ballot this November Massachusetts Question 3: Measure on the ballot would end party primaries Massachusetts Question 4: Should same-day voter registration be allowed? Massachusetts Question 5: Voters asked whether to cap state revenue growth Massachusetts Question 6: Will voters approve creating 'Nature for All Fund'? Massachusetts Question 7: Voters to decide on new state rules for single-family homes on small lots Massachusetts Question 8: Retail marijuana shops back on the ballot 10 years after legalization Massachusetts Question 9: Voters asked to decide on recent updates to state gun laws U.S. House
 Democrats are seeking to defend all nine of the state's seats in the U.S. House as the party seeks to gain control of the chamber in this midterm election.
 The state's eight Democratic incumbents - Rep. Richard Neal, Rep. James McGovern, Rep. Lori Trahan, Rep. Jake Auchincloss, Rep. Katherine Clark, Rep. Ayanna Pressley and Rep. Stephen Lynch - are all running for reelection. Clark, McGovern and Pressley are unopposed.
 Only one of the state's nine seats in the U.S. House is open. In that District 6 race, Democrat Dan Koh faces Republican Micah Quinney Jones .
 Koh, who worked in the Biden White House and was Chief of Staff to Boston Mayor Marty Walsh, said his first priority in office would be investigating "corruption" in the Trump administration.
 Jones, a U.S. Army veteran and attorney, said his first priority would be preventing members of Congress from trading individual stocks.
 Other races on the ballot
 Attorney General
 Secretary of State
 Treasurer
 Auditor
 Governor’s Councilor
 State Senator
 State Representative
 District Attorney
 Register of Probate
 County Commissioner (certain counties only)
 County Treasurer (certain counties only)
 Sheriff (Franklin County – to fill vacancy)
 Additional local offices (vary by community)
 Where to vote
 Polling places will be open Tuesday from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
 To find your polling place, enter your street address into THIS TOOL from the Secretary of the Commonwealth's office.
 Who can vote
 There is no same-day registration for voters in Massachusetts, although one of the questions on the ballot could change that.
 Voters are required to register 10 days before an election. In this case, the deadline was 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 24.
 Those who requested a mail-in ballot can still vote in person if:
 You applied to vote by mail, but never returned your ballot
 You mailed your ballot back, but it hasn’t reached your local election office
 Your ballot was received by your local election office, but it was rejected
 Polls close at 8 p.m., but anyone already in line before the deadline will be allowed to vote. Tabulation of ballots begins only after polls close.
